winning_patterns.description: Top performers utilize 'aspect_ratio: square' and lead with specific, low-barrier price points or free offers in the 'hook_text' and 'price_visible' fields, whereas bottom performers hide pricing.

Winning ads use high-contrast 'dominant_colors' like orange or light green against neutral backgrounds to create a 'pattern_interrupt: true' visual, while bottom ads use more muted or generic blue/white palettes.
The presence of 'has_celebrity: true' or high-status aspirational copy tied to specific low price points (₹99) drives higher performance than generic functional benefits.

losing_patterns.description: Consistently, ads with 'aspect_ratio: portrait' appear in the bottom performers, suggesting the creative layout or platform placement for this format is not resonating as well as square assets.
Bottom performers rely on the exact same 'hook_text' ('Built for the bold. Designed for the driven.') which lacks a specific 'value_proposition' or 'discount_present', leading to lower engagement.
Ads focusing on 'tone: functional' and solving technical problems (foggy lenses) without a strong financial 'offer' or 'discount_type' underperform compared to style-led ads.

patterns.brand_creative_signature: Lenskart's creative style is defined by high-saturation, product-focused lifestyle photography that emphasizes color-coordinated frames against clean, minimalist backgrounds. They rely on a mix of aspirational 'boardroom' messaging and aggressive 'Buy 1 Get 1' or entry-level pricing hooks to drive conversion.
patterns.biggest_gap: Complete absence of 'has_ugc', 'has_reviews', or 'has_ratings' across all 10 ads, missing a massive opportunity to build trust through social proof.

ideas.hook_concept: A customer unboxing a premium-looking frame with a text overlay saying 'I only paid ₹99 for these.'
ideas.visual_brief: A 1:1 square video featuring a selfie-style unboxing. The bottom third of the frame should feature a persistent '₹99' price tag in a high-contrast orange bubble.
ideas.hypothesis: Addressing the 'Biggest Gap' (UGC/Social Proof) while leveraging 'Pattern 1' (Price Anchoring) will build the trust necessary to convert low-price offers.

ideas.hook_concept: A celebrity wearing neon-framed glasses against a high-contrast vibrant orange background.
ideas.headline_draft: Look Like a Star for Just ₹999.
ideas.visual_brief: Square format featuring a high-saturation orange background. Use a celebrity image with high-status styling, ensuring the eyewear color (e.g., light green) creates a 'pattern_interrupt' against the background.
ideas.hypothesis: Combines 'Pattern 2' (Vibrant Color Contrast) with 'Pattern 3' (Celebrity Signaling) to maximize scroll-stop and aspirational value.

ideas.hook_concept: Large 5-star rating stars appearing over the first frame's product with '1M+ Happy Customers' text.
ideas.visual_brief: 1:1 square cards. Card 1 shows a best-selling frame with a '4.9/5' star badge and '₹99' price anchor. Subsequent cards show different styles with short 1-line customer testimonials.
ideas.hypothesis: Directly solves the 'Biggest Gap' (Social Proof) while maintaining the winning 'Pattern 1' (Square format & aggressive price anchoring).

ideas.hook_concept: Large, bold 'FREE' or '₹0' text in light green on a dark neutral background.
ideas.headline_draft: Your First Frame is on Us!
ideas.visual_brief: Square layout with a minimalist shot of a premium frame centered. Surround the frame with a vibrant light green geometric border that pops against a dark grey background to draw eyes to the price.
ideas.hypothesis: Uses 'Pattern 2' (Color Contrast) to draw immediate attention to the 'Pattern 1' (Aggressive Price Anchor) of the 'Free' offer.

ideas.hook_concept: Creator says 'How I look like a CEO on a budget' while putting on Lenskart glasses.
ideas.visual_brief: A 'Get Ready With Me' style video where a creator transitions from casual to professional. Include a 'Verified Buyer' badge and a '4.8 Star' overlay in the top right corner.
ideas.hypothesis: Merges 'Pattern 3' (Status Signaling/Boardroom messaging) with the 'Biggest Gap' (UGC/Social Proof) to make the aspirational lifestyle feel attainable and trustworthy.
